memory_candidates.content: BimodalLogic's specs/ROADMAP.md is a STAGE-layout roadmap under scripts/roadmap-integration.sh: in that mode every '## ' section is retained byte-for-byte EXCEPT the single section whose body holds a fenced /orchestrate block ('## Run these next'), which is re-rendered wholly from specs/state.json's roadmap_batches/roadmap_notes. So a hand edit to any OTHER section (e.g. '## Where both fronts now stand', '## Stage 0', '## Next batches') is durable and is the correct edit target, while a hand edit inside '## Run these next' is silently overwritten by the next regeneration. The cheap, exit-status-checkable proof that a hand edit landed in a retained region is 'bash .claude/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate --dry-run', which prints 'layout=stage ... retained=N' plus either 'no content change' or a diff -- a far better covering check for a ROADMAP.md prose edit than any shell suite, since suite_selection_select maps specs/ROADMAP.md to only 4 roadmap-generation suites and specs/state.json to 76 (every suite that READS state.json, i.e. effectively a full sweep).
